title: The Magazine Welcomes New Staff Members and an Exciting Slate of Contributing Writers
summary: The team welcomes a designer, “Cannonball” and several contributing writers.
body_markdown:
The team welcomes a designer, “Cannonball” and several contributing writers. Read more from the Magazine’s editor, Jake Silverstein.


The New York Times Magazine is pleased to announce several exciting new additions to its staff and roster of contributing writers.


The Magazine’s art department is pleased to welcome a new designer, Siri Lee. Siri comes to The Times from MoMA, where she designed across a wide range of major exhibitions, brand campaigns and publications. Before her time at MoMA, she designed and developed print and web projects for various arts and cultural organizations, including Columbia University’s Graduate School of Architecture, Planning and Preservation, the Smart Museum of Art in Chicago and the Yale Center Beijing.


“Cannonball,” the weekly culture show hosted by Wesley Morris that launched last year, is now based at the Magazine. That means that Janelle Anderson and John White, two talented producers for the show, have joined the Magazine staff. Janelle worked with Wesley in the past on his unforgettable[Stevie Wonder podcast](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-wonder-of-stevie/id1767486783) , and John previously worked at Gimlet Media — where he produced narrative hits like “[Crimetown](https://open.spotify.com/show/5C9yXrX999QNS1Q62IlXvc) ” and “[Conviction](https://open.spotify.com/show/2XquJlPU9ibLYZMH0ZzFwA) .” Both Janelle and John will be valuable additions to the Magazine, not only for their work on “Cannonball,” but also for their contributions to its broader culture coverage.


The Magazine is also pleased to welcome several new contributing writers:


- **Billy Brennan** last wrote for the Magazine about[remarkable moments of lucidity among dementia patients](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/14/magazine/terminal-lucidity.html) as they near death. He also wrote a piece about[the Mews](https://www.nytimes.com/2020/08/20/magazine/teeth-mewing-incels.html) , a father-and-son duo of orthodontists who have proposed an unconventional explanation for dental misalignment. His story for the Washingtonian[about a man who dug a secret tunnel system in the D.C. suburbs](https://washingtonian.com/2019/09/08/paranoid-tech-bro-homemade-nuclear-bunker-shocking-death-askia-khafra-daniel-beckwitt/) won a National City and Regional Magazine Award for feature writing. He has also written for The Atlantic and The New Yorker, and was a co-executive producer on the Netflix docuseries “Worst Roommate Ever,” which was adapted from[his New York magazine article](https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/jamison-bachman-worst-roommate-ever.html) of the same name.
- **Christopher Cox** ’s stories for the Magazine have examined[Elon Musk’s false claims about Tesla’s self-driving technology](https://www.nytimes.com/2023/01/17/magazine/tesla-autopilot-self-driving-elon-musk.html) , uncovered the surprising[vulnerability of California’s dams](https://www.nytimes.com/2023/06/22/magazine/california-dams.html) and presented a[new narrative of the Lewis and Clark expedition](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/07/23/magazine/sacagawea-biography-history.html) that radically revises our understanding of Sacagawea. His most recent feature, about[threats to the U.S. electric grid](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/18/magazine/national-blackout-power-electricity-outage.html) , was one of our most popular stories this year. He was formerly the chief editor of Harper’s Magazine and executive editor of GQ. He is also the author of “The Deadline Effect.”
- **Daniel Kolitz** is a writer living in Brooklyn whose latest piece for the Magazine went[inside the microdrama industry in Hollywood](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/06/magazine/microdramas-tv-shows-hollywood-entertainment.html) . Last year, he won the National Magazine Award in feature writing for “The Goon Squad” in Harper’s Magazine.
- **Benjamin Wallace** wrote this summer’s memorable (and horrifying) Magazine[cover story on ticks](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/20/magazine/tick-season-lone-star-alpha-gal-syndrome-lyme.html) , and has also written for the daily report, including a story on[A.I.-enabled boom times for philosophy majors](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/05/business/philosophy-majors-ai-jobs.html) and an early look at the[rise of prediction markets](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/22/business/prediction-markets-polymarket-kalshi.html) . Ben has been a feature writer at New York magazine and a contributing editor at Vanity Fair. He is the author of “The Mysterious Mr. Nakamoto: A Fifteen-Year Quest to Unmask the Secret Genius Behind Crypto” and “The Billionaire’s Vinegar: The Mystery of the World’s Most Expensive Bottle of Wine.”


Please join us in congratulating everyone.
